html:
Cecil Rhodes was an English-born mining magnate and politician in southern Africa, and the most forceful promoter of the British Empire there in the late 1800s.

He came to Natal in 1870 for his health and soon went to the diamond fields of the Kimberley rush. By buying up claims he built De Beers, which came to control most of the world's diamonds. He also made money from gold on the Witwatersrand.

  • In 1889 he won a royal charter for the British South Africa Company. Its settlers occupied Shona country in 1890 and its troops crushed the Ndebele kingdom in 1893. The land was named Rhodesia after him.
  • He was prime minister of the Cape Colony from 1890 to 1896. His Glen Grey Act of 1894 limited African land holding and pushed men into wage work.
  • He backed the Jameson Raid of 1895 to 1896, a failed plot to overthrow the Boer government of the Transvaal. It forced him out of office and helped bring on the Boer War.

He dreamed of British rule from the Cape to Cairo, joined by a railway. He died in 1902 and was buried in the Matobo Hills. His will paid for the Rhodes Scholarships at Oxford, and his land below Table Mountain went to the University of Cape Town. In 2015 the Rhodes Must Fall protests there got his statue removed.
